data.title: Blastoise Pokémon Card Sells for $630,000, Setting Record as Crypto Markets Slump
data.description: A CGC 8.5 NM-MT+ 1998 Commissioned Presentation Galaxy Holo Blastoise sold for $630,000 at Fanatics Collect, setting an all-time record for a Blastoise card and more than doubling the previous high of $241,083.60. The card, one of two known copies made to promote the Pokémon Trading Card Game to North American retailers, sold as Bitcoin hit a 21-month low and spot ETFs recorded heavy outflows, according to BeInCrypto. A 1996 Japanese Blastoise graded PSA 10 had previously sold for $231,800 and now ranks third; Charizard remains the most valuable Kanto starter, with a recent public sale of a Base Set Shadowless 1st Edition Charizard PSA 10 reaching $954,800. Pokémon was the best-selling U.S. toy brand in 2025, with $2.5 billion in sales. On-chain spending on tokenized cards reached a record $324 million in June 2026, more than 5x the year-earlier figure. Courtyard and Collector Crypt offer tokens backed by graded cards; Courtyard burns 5% to 8% of its tokens weekly through redemptions, about 30% of Collector Crypt users claim their cards, and Collector Crypt has tokenized roughly $40 million worth of cards.

data.title: Former Aave DAO Core Member Marc Zeller Is Shorting AAVE, Up About $248,000
data.description:
Former Aave DAO core member and Acier founder Marc Zeller is shorting AAVE and had about $248,000 in profit at the time of a screenshot.

According to Odaily, Nansen CEO Alex Svanevik posted a screenshot of an address on X showing the position and profit. Zeller later confirmed in a comment that he was shorting AAVE.

Zeller previously founded the Aave Chan Initiative (ACI) and was a longtime core participant in Aave DAO governance. He and Aave founder Stani Kulechov and associated teams came to differ over the DAO’s governance model, allocation of decision-making authority and the direction of ecosystem development as Kulechov’s group gained influence. Zeller later gradually withdrew from the Aave ecosystem and founded the lending project Acier.

data.description: Citrea will begin its Pomelo mainnet upgrade today at 11:00 PM. data.title: Faculty Group's Yaroslav Writtle: RWA Lending May Be More Profitable Than Tokenization
data.description:
RWA platforms may earn more by financing tokenized assets than by issuing and managing them, argues Faculty Group partner Yaroslav Writtle. According to Foresight News, the industry has focused for years on putting assets such as government bonds, private credit, real estate and corporate debt on-chain, but financing those assets could offer a larger revenue opportunity.

Tokenization providers typically earn issuance, management and custody fees, often tied to assets under management or services provided. Lenders, by contrast, earn interest and fees and can redeploy capital as loans are repaid, generating revenue across the credit cycle.

Warehouse financing offers one model: a funding provider advances capital to a lender against eligible loans or receivables, allowing the lender to issue new loans before existing borrowers repay. Stablecoin capital could provide another source of funding, linking investors seeking returns with businesses that need money for lending, inventory or invoice financing. Tokenization can improve collateral records, reporting and settlement, but the core economic value comes from connecting funding with borrowers.

In November, Securitize acquired River One, which specializes in warehouse financing and credit underwriting. The move extends Securitize’s activities beyond tokenization infrastructure into credit origination, financing and loan management. Other platforms have connected tokenized credit to lending markets through protocols including Morpho and Kamino.

Lending can produce higher returns, but it also exposes platforms to borrower and collateral risks, liquidity management and defaults. Interest income must cover funding and operating costs as well as credit losses, and tokenization does not improve a borrower’s creditworthiness. Writtle expects more RWA platforms to engage in financing or credit portfolio management, while noting that their ability to manage underlying risks will be important.

data.title: STOCKS | South Korean Finance Minister Lee Hyeong-il Says Market Measures May Boost Investor Confidence, Government to Study Stabilization Fund
data.description:
South Korean Finance Minister Lee Hyeong-il said the government’s commitment to stabilizing the stock market is expected to improve investor sentiment. According to Odaily, the government will study procedures for launching a stock market stabilization fund, with specific measures to be determined based on market conditions. Lee said South Korea’s short-selling rules are stricter than those in other markets and that the government will focus on monitoring illegal short selling.

Lee said economic growth this year is expected to be in the upper end of the 3% range, with 4% technically possible. He expects steady growth to continue in 2027, while stable global oil prices could help bring inflation down. External risks remain high, including AI industry regulation, geopolitical conditions and high global interest rates; semiconductor industry volatility could also affect the broader economy.

Lee said a sustained current account surplus would bring the won closer to its fundamentals, but declined to comment on the currency’s current level. The government plans to announce measures to strengthen the electric vehicle industry this week and, starting next year, increase the frequency of its economic growth forecasts from twice to three times a year.

data.title: MSCI CEO Discussed Ways to Avoid Indonesia Downgrade With Prabowo, Dalio

data.title: South Korea to Tighten Oversight of Crypto Transfers Abroad and Personal Wallets
data.description: South Korean Financial Services Commission Chairman Lee Eok-won reiterated that authorities would crack down on money laundering involving cryptocurrency transactions. According to Odaily, under implementing rules for the Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information, revised in August, regulators will strengthen reporting and review requirements for virtual asset service providers and closely monitor transfers to high-risk overseas exchanges and personal wallets.

data.title: MSCI CEO Henry Fernandez Open to Alternatives to Two-Step Downgrade of Indonesia’s Stock Market Classification

data.title: AI TRENDS | Visa Launches Experimental AI Agent Wallet Visa CLI for U.S. Users
data.description: Visa has launched its experimental AI agent wallet, Visa CLI, for users in the United States. According to Odaily, the wallet is built on Tempo and the Machine Payments Protocol (MPP). Cuy Sheffield, head of Visa Crypto Labs, said Visa has extended its Trusted Agent Protocol (TAP) and Visa Agent Directory to agent wallets and task marketplaces, with Visa CLI and Taskmarket among the first supported. Users can connect a wallet, link a bank card, use the card to verify an AI agent’s identity, and register the agent in the Visa Agent Directory. Visa-verified agents can take paid tasks in video production, music creation, gaming, paid surveys and market research, and earn OUSD.

data.title: Cross-Market Liquidity Tightening Adds Oil Selling Pressure, but Rebound Risk Remains
data.description: According to Jin10, easing geopolitical risk premiums and tightening liquidity in technology stocks combined to intensify selling pressure on oil prices. Downstream oil markets remain tight, and frequent tanker attacks in the strait suggest risks have not been resolved. Investment banks expect crude oil could still rebound.
